body:
Coordinator rule (Termal::Fable2, 2026-10-31 12:05Z), learned from two slips today on Engram B's a845 batch and the w-18af 7066 batch. When giving a remote runner a named GO, especially an advance GO before the author's job reaches the runner, do NOT spell out a command form of my own (for example 'eight separate focused launchers' or 'two serial launcher runs'). Authors package batches their own way: one focused launcher run of a .sh or .ps1 recipe. My restated form then conflicts with theirs, and careful runners correctly HOLD for reconciliation, which costs a round trip.
Rule: in the GO, name the input identity (commit, tree, parent, bundle or patch sha), the conditions (fresh clean root, own target, census limits such as load ≤4 on the Mac), stop-at-first-failure/no-retry, and notify. For the commands, say 'exactly as the author's job specifies'.
Related: before moving a job to another lane, confirm where it is already prepared. A lane flip on crossing messages (B a845 Windows B → DL560 → back) risks a duplicate.
